claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation is governed by grain-boundary stabilization through dopant-induced solute drag.
Dopant-induced solute drag inhibits grain-boundary sliding.
Dopant-induced solute drag inhibits dislocation climb.
The proposed CoCrFeMnNi-based multilayers have an alternating-layer, fine-grained nanocrystalline microstructure.
Minor Ti or Nb additions enhance grain-boundary stability in these multilayers.
Grain-boundary mobility is an important factor under sustained loading at 350–450 °C.
Transient creep in the nanocrystalline multilayer architecture at elevated temperature is mediated by grain-boundary sliding.
Transient creep in the nanocrystalline multilayer architecture at elevated temperature is mediated by dislocation climb.
Introducing dopants into selected layers stabilizes grain boundaries by creating a solute-drag effect.
Doped multilayers with stabilized grain boundaries will have lower creep rates than undoped baseline multilayers.
Doped multilayers with stabilized grain boundaries will accumulate less plastic strain than undoped baseline multilayers.
Enhanced grain-boundary stability will correlate with suppressed plastic deformation.
Removing the grain-boundary-stabilizing dopants while retaining otherwise identical deposition conditions produces a coarser or less stable grain structure.
The proposed mechanism is most applicable at 350–450 °C when grain-boundary sliding and dislocation climb dominate deformation.
The proposed mechanism may not explain lower-temperature deformation or regimes dominated by other mechanisms.
